shared_context.content: For noncollinear points A,B,C in the Euclidean plane R^2, write circumcenter(A,B,C) for the unique point O in R^2 such that OA = OB = OC; equivalently O is the intersection point of the perpendicular bisectors of AB and AC.
shared_context.label: Circumcenter notation

shared_context.content: For a function f : R^2 -> {red,green} and a color c in {red,green}, write S_c = { P in R^2 | f(P) = c }.
shared_context.label: Color classes

strategy_summary: Reduce the coloring statement to a structural theorem about a single color class viewed as a subset of the plane that is closed under taking circumcenters of noncollinear triples. Then prove that some color class must contain a noncollinear triple, and invoke the structural theorem to conclude that this color class is the whole plane.
